summary: Make pool ID, pool name and host ID host-owned: the agent generates them on first enrollment, keeps them in its state, and presents them at every enrollment so any Controller, including a fresh replacement, adopts them unchanged. The Controller validates the presented identity, refuses claims on identities already on record, replays the recorded credential for a same-key retry, and still mints IDs for older agents.

guide.reason: Replacing a failed Controller now brings each pool back with its original ID and name and each master with its original host ID; the manage-controller troubleshooting entry said each master landed in a new pool named after its hostname.

api.reason: API impact: changed contract. POST /api/v1/agent/enroll: EnrollRequest gains optional host_id, pool_id and pool_name (host-generated, validated as UUID or legacy 64-hex, name rule), EnrollResponse gains pool_id and pool_name; new 400 for invalid identity and 409 for a host or pool identity already on record or not matching a replacement token; same-key retry replays the recorded credential. Older agents that present nothing keep the previous minted behaviour. OpenAPI contract and generated reference updated; docs/API.md documents the rules and compatibility.

state.reason: Pool ID, pool name and host ID are generated by the host and durably kept in the agent state on the pool master; the Controller only mirrors what the host presents.
state.record: Agent state.json on the pool master (host_id, pool_id, pool_name; pending_host_id until first acceptance). A fresh Controller recovers them from the host's ordinary enrollment request (POST /api/v1/agent/enroll presents host_id, pool_id, pool_name), then adopts the managed journal under that pool and host.

verification.method: go build ./... && go test ./... passing (internal/agent: host generates and persists identity before the request, retry presents the same, replacement Controller keeps host/pool identity with a fresh credential and cleared journal, legacy host adopts the reported pool, a Controller changing the host identity is refused; internal/controller TestHostOwnedIdentity: presented identity adopted and visible in hosts/pools with certificate CN, same-key retry with a new token replays, active host and held pool claims 409, invalid UUID/uppercase/name 400, legacy enrollment still minted, replacement token must present the same host and pool, a second fresh Controller adopts the same identity; internal/localcore enrollment tests against fakes that echo the presented identity). python3 -m unittest tests.test_agent_service tests.test_api_contract passing after the OpenAPI update; python3 scripts/generate_api.py regenerated the reference. tests/integration/controller_replacement.py now asserts host_id, pool_id and pool name are preserved across Controller A -> B; run locally 2026-09-10 as root inside sudo unshare -nm with prebuilt binaries on loopback (no --vm, so no libvirt; VM definitions covered by Controller unit tests only): both checks PASS, evidence shows the same host UUID, pool UUID and pool name on Controller A and on the empty replacement Controller B, adoption under that pool/host with no command dispatched and no duplicates. python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree passing.
